title: LS-MDRM Transition Manual
description: Defines the transition vocabulary, transformation rules, and conditions for valid recursive Lens Shift transitions.

productive.label: EXPAND
productive.definition: The successor state broadens scope, adds new dimensions, or introduces additional causal candidates relative to the predecessor.

productive.label: NARROW
productive.definition: The successor state restricts scope, removes candidates, or sharpens discriminability.

productive.label: ABSTRACT
productive.definition: The successor state moves to a higher level of generality, retaining causal linkage to predecessor.

productive.label: GROUND
productive.definition: The successor state adds, strengthens, or revises evidence binding for a prior claim.

productive.label: INVERT
productive.definition: The successor state reverses a prior causal or inferential direction, retaining predecessor acknowledgment.

productive.label: BRANCH
productive.definition: The successor state forks from a predecessor, producing a candidate set under the branch lifecycle protocol.

productive.label: REVISE
productive.definition: The successor state corrects a prior erroneous claim with explicit acknowledgment.

productive.label: OPERATIONALIZE
productive.definition: The successor state converts an abstract hypothesis into a specific, testable claim.

productive.label: COMPRESS
productive.definition: The successor state reduces complexity burden without losing material content.

failure_degeneration.label: JUMP
failure_degeneration.definition: The successor state introduces a new topic or claim without traceable predecessor ancestry.
failure_degeneration.detection: P < 2 at successor state and no branch record exists.

failure_degeneration.label: RESTATE
failure_degeneration.definition: The successor state is semantically equivalent to the predecessor.
failure_degeneration.detection: R >= 3 at successor state and C <= 1.

failure_degeneration.label: STALL
failure_degeneration.definition: No transition occurs; the state is copied without meaningful change.
failure_degeneration.detection: Transition operator absent or empty; state n+1 identical to state n.

multi_label_rule: A single transition may carry multiple labels. All applicable labels must be recorded. Do not force a transition into a single category if multiple apply.
successor_qualification_rule: A successor state may be intelligent or relevant without qualifying as recursive Lens Shift. Traceable predecessor ancestry is required. P >= 3 is the minimum for a transition to qualify as recursive.

recursive_transition_formula.description: S_{n+1} = R(S_n, tau_n, B_n^raw, B_n^eligible, B_n^selected, E_n; Z, Theta)
constraints: tau_n must be in Consequences(S_n): the transition must follow from predecessor tensions, not from arbitrary selection.
B_n^selected must be in B_n^eligible, which must be a subset of B_n^raw.
E_n must be bound to a corpus version at the bound commit.
